label: sequence began with l: original steps t>=3 and <DEL>
explanation: Fires in sequences whose first original token is l, at original-phase steps from t=3 on and at the <DEL> step. It holds the memory of l in slot 0 through the encoding phase. Magnitude peaks around t=4-5 and fades with later t; it is near zero by t=8-9, so long sequences show low <DEL> activations. Top activations are on l l x ... sequences (l at positions 0 and 1). The current input token barely matters. It is silent at t=0-1, almost silent at t=2, and essentially never fires in the copy phase (58 steps). Missed activations are weak (9% of mass) and come mostly from sequences with l at position 1 rather than 0, which fire faintly at t=4-6.

issues: Most of the factual claims hold. Firing peaks at t=4: rate 0.058, 33% of mass. It is zero at t=0-1, tiny at t=2 (0.2% of mass) and zero from t>=10. The copy phase has only 58 active steps. first_tok==l carries 90.9% of the mass with 20.7x lift. Test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.925, R 0.679, F1 0.783, mass recall 0.907.

There is a systematic miss class, not scattered noise. The predicate misses 32% of active steps (32,468 on test), and the bottom two activation quartiles have only 16% and 56% coverage. Most of the misses are sequences with l at position 1 but not position 0 (orig(1)==l & first_tok!=l & t>=3 & phase<=1). That class holds 23.8% of all active test steps, at precision 0.33. Active steps with l at neither position 0 nor 1 make up only 6.4% of active steps, and l at position 2 contributes almost nothing (0.15%). So the feature is specifically 'l in slot 0 (strong) or slot 1 (weak)', and the label 'sequence began with l' leaves out a quarter of its firing events.

There is also a systematic false-positive class. The t>=3 clause has no upper bound, but firing dies out by t=9 (180 active steps on dev; zero from t=10). The test false positives shown are all <DEL> steps at t=8-9 in L=8/9 sequences. Capping at t<=8 raises precision from 0.925 to 0.959 with no recall loss, and t<=7 raises it to 0.990. The explanation mentions the fade but the predicate and label do not encode it.

The agent's reason for dropping the second clause ('cut precision to 0.80') is not a good trade-off: a properly bounded two-clause predicate reaches test F1 0.863 vs 0.783, with mass recall 0.986 and precision 0.85.
